newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Mobil Singapore sees reasonable margins in 1Q'97.
newsitem.headline: Mobil Singapore sees reasonable margins in 1Q'97.

text.p: Mobil Oil Singapore, a unit of US oil giant Mobil Corp, said on Friday it expected reasonable margins would be sustained through the first quarter of 1997.

"Winter in the U.S., Europe and China coinciding with low inventory levels are likely to sustain reasonable margins through the first quarter of 1997," a Mobil spokesman said in written response to a Reuter query.
"The fundamentals for crude supply are stable. Volatility in pricing is generally short term and news-driven and therefore hard to predict," the spokesman said.
He said Mobil's Jurong refinery, which has a 280,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) capacity, was running at full capacity for most of the year.
According to earlier reports, Mobil had cut crude runs at its refinery by 10,000 bpd in mid-June when refining margins were poor, and restored it to full capacity by end August.
"Margins have been positive in the last quarter and over the course of the year, have been better than expected, being positive for eight out of 12 months," the spokesman said.
Mobil said it estimates a three-to-four-percent growth in oil products demand for Asia in 1997.
"Over the longer term, regional demand will continue to be healthy but we foresee that it would probably take around three years for regional demand to outpace supply."

The spokesman said marginal new capacities coming on stream in 1997 from debottlenecking in China and Japan would cater for internal consumption and would not have any significant impact on the international market.
